title: midday-shift-bridge-synthesis-2026-03-15
body:
Shift: Midday (11:00-15:00 PDT), 2026-03-15
Owner on shift: Maya Chen (primary), Diego Alvarez (secondary)
Summary: short, actionable summary for next shift
- Primary event: transient serving degradation observed in hosted-api model-serving tier between 10:42–11:30 PDT causing elevated 5xx rates and tail latency spikes for text-generation endpoints. Impact limited to ~8% of requests during peak window. No customer data exposure.
- Mitigation: traffic throttles and autoscaler adjustments applied; a targeted rollback for the 2026-03-15.1 service-builder image at 10:55 PDT reduced error rate to baseline by 11:20 PDT.
- Escalation: alerted infra platform oncall (Priya R.) at 10:50 PDT due to suspected autoscaler misconfiguration; SRE lead looped at 11:05 PDT.
- Current state at end of shift: service stable, autoscaler config corrected in staging, permanent fix in progress (JIRA SRE-4821). Monitoring remains on heightened watch for next 24 hours.

Incidents observed (ordered by severity)
1) Incident: hosted-api model-serving 5xx spike
- Temporal window: 2026-03-15 10:42–11:30 PDT
- Symptoms: sudden increase in 502/503s from model prod pool B; 99th p90 latency up from 280ms to ~2.4s for short prompts; request queueing observed on worker nodes.
- Signals reviewed: grafana panels (req/sec, cpu% per pod, queue length), logs (gateway x-forwarded-for traces), autoscaler metrics (target desired_replicas vs actual).
- Immediate actions:
  * 10:46 PDT — Started bridge channel, initial triage (Maya).
  * 10:50 PDT — Disabled request batching at gateway for pool B as an emergency mitigation (reduced queue pressure).
  * 10:53 PDT — Triggered controlled rollback to previous service-builder image (2026-03-15.1).
  * 10:55 PDT — Escalated to platform oncall (Priya) due to inconsistent desired_replicas calculation.
  * 11:04 PDT — Confirmed that rollback is progressing; new pods started with older image.
  * 11:20 PDT — Error rate returned to acceptable baseline (<0.5% 5xx); latency normalized.
- Root cause hypothesis (interim): autoscaler config bug combined with aggressive new image change in 2026-03-15.2 that increased memory footprint under specific input-length distribution, causing pods to hit OOM/killed cycles and triggering cascading downstream 502s.
- Evidence/rationale: increased OOMKilled counts on nodes hosting pool B, heap growth traces in the sidecar logs for 2026-03-15.2 image, and a correlated spike in desired_replicas miscalculation (scaler reported negative headroom).
- Runbooks consulted: "model-serving/rollback-and-deploy.md" and "autoscaler/debugging-checklist.md". These were partially sufficient but lacked a check for the new image's memory profile in the scaler health probe.
- Tickets opened: JIRA SRE-4821 (investigate root cause + fix autoscaler logic), and infra PR reference GH#978 for a temporary autoscaler guard.

2) Follow-on: monitoring alert noise and pager churn
- Several non-actionable alerts fired during the incident (high memory on control-plane monitors). We suppressed noisy alerts at 11:15 PDT but recorded their sources to avoid losing telemetry.
- Action: create a separate alert rule for transient OOM bursts so rotations aren't woken for short-lived spikes. Assigned Diego to SRE-4826.

Operational notes and decisions made on bridge
- We prioritized availability over throughput: disabled gateway batching for affected pool to reduce queue head-of-line blocking. Note: this temporarily increases per-token cost.
- Decided against a full cluster scale-up as evidence pointed to per-pod resource regressions, not cluster-wide capacity shortage.
- Temporary access: we allowed platform oncall to run memory-profile diagnostic job on pool B; logs placed in S3: s3://redwood-ops/diagnostics/2026-03-15/poolB-memory-profiles.tar.gz

What went well
- Quick detection: observability dashboards and synthetic checks caught the regression within 3 minutes of onset.
- Clear triage: bridge established, ownership clear, rollback executed within ~10 minutes of escalation.
- Good communication: Slack thread summarized updates every ~8 minutes; customer-facing status page updated at 11:08 PDT.

What needs improvement / action items (short term)
- Add image memory-profile validation to the pre-release checklist for service-builder images (owner: Alex Kim; due: 2026-03-22).
- Update autoscaler runbook to include a "validate desired_replicas" quick check and explicit guidance for negative headroom cases (owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-18).
- Reduce alert noise: create transient-oom alert suppression window or timing rule (owner: Diego; JIRA SRE-4826; due: 2026-03-20).
- CI: add a smoke test to exercise short prompt latency distribution in staging for new model images (owner: ML infra; ticket: MLINFRA-109).

Longer-term follow-ups (medium term)
- Root cause RCA write-up: assign to SRE-4821 with input from serving-runtime and applied-ml. Target: 2026-03-29.
- Autoscaler refactor: add headroom sanity checks and limit enforcement for sudden memory regressions; plan design doc (owner: infra; due: 2026-04-12).
- Cost analysis of batching toggle decisions: quantify delta in per-token cost vs. availability improvement and propose automated policy for future incidents (owner: product-optimize; due: 2026-04-05).

Open action items (with owners)
- Maya: attach selected logs and heapdumps to SRE-4821 (done, link in ticket).
- Priya: push autoscaler guard PR to infra repo (GH#978 opened, needs review).
- Diego: create alert tuning ticket SRE-4826 and propose suppression parameters (in progress).
- Alex: draft pre-release memory-profile checklist and share in #release-process for review.

Notes to next shift (succinct)
- Monitor pool B closely for next 24 hours; watch OOMKilled and desired_replicas discrepancy panels.
- Do not re-enable gateway batching on pool B until both autoscaler guard and image memory checks are merged.
- If 5xx > 1% for more than 10 minutes, escalate to platform oncall immediately and consider a scoped full rollback for other pools.

Artifacts/links to review during next shift
- Grafana: model-serving/pool-B-overview dashboard -> panel ids: 3,4,7
- JIRA: SRE-4821, SRE-4826
- GH: infra PR #978 (autoscaler guard), infra issue #981 (autoscaler edgecases)
- Confluence: Autoscaler Investigation Notes page (link above)

Meeting / post-incident plan
- Quick sync scheduled with applied-ml and serving-runtime tomorrow 2026-03-16 09:30 PDT (calendar invite sent to eng-sre, applied-ml, infra).
- RCA doc to be drafted in Confluence; SRE lead will review before wider distribution.

Random notes / scratch (keep for audit)
- Observed unusual spike in long-prompt traffic at 10:40 PDT, origin appears to be a single customer key (cid-9982). We contacted account team for temp throttling consideration if recurrence happens.
- Grepped logs for sidecar memory warnings: found 14 warnings between 10:44–10:52 PDT; saved to /tmp/sre-2026-03-15-sidecar-warnings.log (artifacts attached to ticket).

Appendix: quick checklist for next shift handoff
- Confirm alerts (OOMKilled, 5xx, desired_replicas) are green, or list current counts.
- Verify autoscaler guard PR status; if merged, note commit SHA.
- Confirm Alex's pre-release checklist is available in docs and linked from the ticket.
- Keep PD escalation path handy: PD-13724 -> infra -> sre-lead.

Signed: Maya Chen (midday bridge owner)
End of midday-shift-synthesis.
